recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not change ElementDefinition.base to 1..1 without a new FHIR-I decision explicitly requiring base in all ElementDefinition contexts, including differentials.
issue_request: FHIR-12295 was Published/Persuasive and asked to make ElementDefinition.base mandatory for tooling consistency, especially to expose original cardinality for XML/JSON conversion, and to remove the sentence limiting base information to non-original element definitions.
initial_application: The explicit application commit 895710265113b796cb75d13c9abf5cfe4aabf207 removed the old limiting sentence and added text that base information must always be populated in snapshot element definitions, while leaving ElementDefinition.base at 0..1.
additional_context: ElementDefinition and StructureDefinition are active current-build artifacts. ElementDefinition is reused by both StructureDefinition.snapshot.element and StructureDefinition.differential.element, so the datatype-level ElementDefinition.base cardinality remains 0..1. Current StructureDefinition source applies sdf-8b only to snapshots, requiring element.all(base.exists()). FHIR-9641 and FHIR-15929 are related supporting decisions in the same base/snapshot rule family; FHIR-15929 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was made because the old sentence is gone, snapshot prose says base must always be populated, and StructureDefinition.snapshot enforces base.exists() for all snapshot elements. A global 1..1 change would overconstrain differential elements.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published clarification that ElementDefinition.base should be populated for inherited elements included in snapshots.

Later Published issue split the StructureDefinition snapshot invariant so 'All snapshot elements must have a base definition' could be enforced independently; already represented on the combined branch.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I issue requesting ElementDefinition.base be mandatory for tooling consistency and removal of the limiting sentence about non-original element definitions.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final seed request and the tooling-driven purpose of the change.

evidence_items.summary: ElementDefinition.base is 0..1, the old limiting sentence is gone, and the comment says base information must always be populated in snapshot element definitions.
evidence_items.learned: The active ElementDefinition source contains the applied snapshot-level requirement without globally mandating base for every ElementDefinition use.

evidence_items.summary: StructureDefinition.snapshot defines sdf-8b, 'All snapshot elements must have a base definition', with expression element.all(base.exists()), and snapshot.element declares that condition.
evidence_items.learned: The current StructureDefinition source enforces mandatory base in the snapshot context needed by tools.

evidence_items.summary: GF#12295 application commit changed the ElementDefinition.base prose and added the snapshot population statement while leaving ElementDefinition.base cardinality at 0..1.
evidence_items.learned: Historical application matches the current contextual implementation and does not support an unqualified 1..1 datatype change.

evidence_items.summary: StructureDefinition.differential.element also uses ElementDefinition but does not carry the sdf-8b base.exists() condition.
evidence_items.learned: A global ElementDefinition.base min-cardinality change would incorrectly apply the snapshot-only rule to differentials.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive issue noting that the StructureDefinition snapshot invariant should be split so 'All snapshot elements must have a base definition' is enforced independently.
evidence_items.learned: Related later WG action supports the current separate snapshot base-definition invariant.
